subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Who created the heavens and the earth?
options: God|Moses|Abraham|David
rubric: Genesis opens with God creating the heavens and the earth.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: On which day did God create man?
options: Third day|Fifth day|Sixth day|Seventh day
rubric: Man was created on the sixth day, after the animals.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: From what did God form the first man?
options: Clay from the river|Dust of the ground|A rib|A tree branch
rubric: God formed Adam from the dust of the ground and breathed life into him.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What did God breathe into man to make him a living being?
options: Water|Fire|Breath of life|Dust
rubric: God breathed into man's nostrils the breath of life (Genesis 2:7).

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Where did God place the first man?
options: Garden of Eden|Mount Sinai|Jerusalem|Egypt
rubric: God planted a garden in Eden and placed Adam there.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Who was the first woman?
options: Sarah|Eve|Mary|Rebecca
rubric: Eve was formed from Adam's rib and became the first woman.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Which tree was Adam forbidden to eat from?
options: Tree of life|Tree of the knowledge of good and evil|Olive tree|Fig tree
answer: Tree of the knowledge of good and evil
rubric: God forbade eating from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Who tempted Eve to disobey God?
options: The serpent|Cain|An angel|Adam
rubric: The serpent deceived Eve and she ate the forbidden fruit.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What did Adam and Eve do when they heard God in the garden?
options: They ran to the gate|They hid themselves|They prayed|They sang
rubric: After sinning they were afraid and hid among the trees.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What did God use to make Eve?
options: A rib from Adam|Dust of the ground|Water|Clay
rubric: God took one of Adam's ribs and formed Eve from it.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What was the first sin committed by man?
options: Murder|Stealing|Disobedience to God|Lying
rubric: The first sin was Adam and Eve's disobedience in eating the forbidden fruit.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What did God make for Adam and Eve before sending them out of Eden?
options: Sandals|Garments of skin|Crowns|Tents
rubric: God clothed them with garments of skin before they left the garden.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: In which town was Jesus born?
options: Nazareth|Bethlehem|Jerusalem|Capernaum
rubric: Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Who was the mother of Jesus?
options: Martha|Mary|Elizabeth|Anna
rubric: Mary was the mother of Jesus.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Who was Jesus' earthly father?
options: Joseph|Zacharias|Simeon|John
rubric: Joseph, a carpenter, was the husband of Mary and earthly father of Jesus.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Who baptised Jesus?
options: Peter|John the Baptist|Paul|James
rubric: John the Baptist baptised Jesus in the River Jordan.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: In which river was Jesus baptised?
options: River Nile|River Jordan|River Benue|River Euphrates
rubric: Jesus was baptised in the River Jordan.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: How many disciples did Jesus choose?
options: Seven|Ten|Twelve|Seventy
rubric: Jesus chose twelve apostles to be his closest followers.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What was Jesus' first miracle?
options: Healing a blind man|Turning water into wine|Walking on water|Feeding five thousand
rubric: At Cana Jesus turned water into wine, his first miracle.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: At which wedding did Jesus perform his first miracle?
options: Cana|Nazareth|Bethany|Jericho
rubric: The miracle took place at a wedding in Cana of Galilee.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Which disciple betrayed Jesus?
options: Peter|Thomas|Judas Iscariot|John
rubric: Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus with a kiss.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: For how much did Judas betray Jesus?
options: Ten pieces of silver|Twenty pieces of silver|Thirty pieces of silver|Fifty pieces of silver
rubric: Judas agreed to betray Jesus for thirty pieces of silver.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Which disciple denied Jesus three times?
options: Peter|Andrew|Philip|Matthew
rubric: Peter denied Jesus three times before the cock crowed.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Where did Jesus pray before his arrest?
options: Garden of Gethsemane|Mount Zion|The temple|Bethany
rubric: Jesus prayed in the Garden of Gethsemane before he was arrested.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Who was forced to carry the cross of Jesus?
options: Simon of Cyrene|Joseph of Arimathea|Nicodemus|Barabbas
rubric: The soldiers forced Simon of Cyrene to carry the cross.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: On which hill was Jesus crucified?
options: Mount Sinai|Golgotha|Mount Carmel|Mount Hermon
rubric: Jesus was crucified at Golgotha, also called Calvary.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: On which day did Jesus rise from the dead?
options: The first day|The second day|The third day|The seventh day
rubric: Jesus rose on the third day, as he had foretold.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What is the ascension?
options: Jesus' birth|Jesus going up to heaven|Jesus' baptism|Jesus' trial
rubric: The ascension is Jesus rising into heaven after his resurrection.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What is the greatest commandment?
options: Do not steal|Love God with all your heart|Honour your parents|Keep the Sabbath
answer: Love God with all your heart
rubric: Jesus said the greatest commandment is to love God with all your heart, soul and mind.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: According to Jesus, who is our neighbour?
options: Only family members|Only fellow Christians|Every person in need|Only friends
rubric: The parable of the Good Samaritan shows our neighbour is anyone in need.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What is the Golden Rule?
options: Do to others as you would have them do to you|Always obey elders|Never speak in public|Give to the rich
answer: Do to others as you would have them do to you
rubric: Jesus taught us to treat others as we want to be treated.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What does forgiveness mean?
options: Punishing a wrongdoer|Letting go of a wrong done to you|Forgetting your friends|Ignoring people
answer: Letting go of a wrong done to you
rubric: Forgiveness means releasing the wrong and not seeking revenge.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Which is the first fruit of the Spirit listed in Galatians?
options: Joy|Peace|Love|Patience
rubric: Galatians 5:22 begins the list of the fruit of the Spirit with love.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What is honesty?
options: Telling the truth always|Making people laugh|Keeping quiet|Working hard
rubric: Honesty means being truthful and sincere in all you do.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Which commandment forbids stealing?
options: You shall not steal|You shall not kill|Honour your father and mother|Remember the Sabbath
rubric: The eighth commandment says, You shall not steal.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Which of these is a fruit of the Spirit?
options: Anger|Patience|Jealousy|Hatred
rubric: Patience is listed among the fruit of the Spirit in Galatians 5:22.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What lesson does the parable of the Good Samaritan teach?
options: Wealth brings happiness|Love your neighbour|Pray without ceasing|Obey the law
rubric: The Samaritan helped a stranger, teaching us to love everyone.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What is prayer?
options: Singing in church|Talking to God|Reading the Bible|Giving offering
rubric: Prayer is communication with God.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What is the Sabbath?
options: A day of work|A day of rest and worship|A feast day|A market day
answer: A day of rest and worship
rubric: The Sabbath is set apart for rest and worship of God.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Honour your father and mother is which commandment?
options: The first|The third|The fifth|The tenth
rubric: Honouring parents is the fifth of the Ten Commandments.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What does creation ex nihilo mean?
options: Creation from water|Creation out of nothing|Creation from dust|Creation by chance
rubric: Ex nihilo is Latin for out of nothing; God created without existing material.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: In whose image was man created?
options: In the image of angels|In God's image|In the image of animals|In the image of Moses
rubric: Genesis says God created man in his own image.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What is original sin?
options: The sin of Cain|The first sin of Adam and Eve passed to humanity|The sin of the Pharisees|The sin of Judas
answer: The first sin of Adam and Eve passed to humanity
rubric: Original sin refers to the disobedience of Adam and Eve inherited by all people.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Who was the first murderer in the Bible?
options: Abel|Seth|Cain|Lamech
rubric: Cain killed his brother Abel out of jealousy.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Whom did Cain kill?
options: Enoch|Abel|Seth|Noah
rubric: Cain killed Abel, the first murder recorded in the Bible.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What was Cain's punishment?
options: He became a fugitive and wanderer|He was killed|He became king|He was sent to Egypt
answer: He became a fugitive and wanderer
rubric: God cursed Cain to be a restless wanderer on the earth.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What did Noah build to save his family from the flood?
options: A temple|An ark|A tower|A wall
rubric: God told Noah to build an ark to save his family and the animals.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What sign did God give after the flood?
options: A star|A rainbow|A dove|A cloud
rubric: The rainbow was the sign of God's covenant with Noah.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What happened at the Tower of Babel?
options: The people were scattered and languages confused|The tower reached heaven|God destroyed the city with fire|The people were blessed
answer: The people were scattered and languages confused
rubric: God confused their language and scattered them over the earth.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What is the incarnation?
options: The belief that God became human in Jesus|The death of Jesus|The baptism of Jesus|The ascension of Jesus
answer: The belief that God became human in Jesus
rubric: Incarnation means God took human flesh in Jesus Christ.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Which angel announced the birth of Jesus to Mary?
options: Michael|Gabriel|Raphael|Uriel
rubric: The angel Gabriel announced to Mary that she would bear Jesus.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: How many days did Jesus fast in the wilderness?
options: Twenty|Thirty|Forty|Fifty
rubric: Jesus fasted forty days and forty nights before being tempted.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Who tempted Jesus in the wilderness?
options: Satan|Peter|Herod|The Pharisees
rubric: The devil tempted Jesus three times in the wilderness.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What is the Sermon on the Mount?
options: A sermon about the temple|Jesus' teaching on a mountain|A sermon by John|A sermon by Peter
rubric: Matthew 5 to 7 records Jesus' teaching on the mountain.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Who appeared with Jesus at the transfiguration?
options: Moses and Elijah|Abraham and Isaac|Peter and John|David and Solomon
rubric: Moses and Elijah appeared with Jesus on the mountain.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Whom did Jesus raise after four days in the tomb?
options: Jairus|Lazarus|Bartimaeus|Malchus
rubric: Jesus raised Lazarus of Bethany on the fourth day.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What did Jesus institute at the Last Supper?
options: The Passover|Holy Communion|Baptism|Confirmations
rubric: Jesus gave his disciples bread and wine as his body and blood.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Who sentenced Jesus to death?
options: Herod Antipas|Pontius Pilate|Caiaphas|Felix
rubric: Pilate, the Roman governor, sentenced Jesus to crucifixion.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What is the Great Commission?
options: Jesus' command to make disciples of all nations|Jesus' command to build a temple|Jesus' command to fast|Jesus' command to pay taxes
answer: Jesus' command to make disciples of all nations
rubric: Before ascending, Jesus sent his followers to make disciples of all nations.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Which parable teaches about different responses to the word of God?
options: The parable of the sower|The parable of the talents|The parable of the lost coin|The parable of the vineyard
rubric: The sower parable describes seed falling on different soils.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What did Jesus teach about forgiveness?
options: Forgive only once|Forgive seventy times seven|Never forgive|Forgive only friends
rubric: Jesus taught that we should forgive without counting.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What is agape love?
options: Romantic love|Selfless unconditional love|Love of money|Love of food
rubric: Agape is the highest form of love, given without conditions.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Which of these is a fruit of the Spirit?
options: Kindness|Greed|Anger|Pride
rubric: Kindness is listed among the fruit of the Spirit.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Blessed are the poor in spirit is part of what teaching?
options: The Beatitudes|The Ten Commandments|The Lord's Prayer|The Golden Rule
rubric: The Beatitudes open the Sermon on the Mount.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What is the Golden Rule?
options: Treat others as you want to be treated|Always obey the rich|Never forgive|Work for money
answer: Treat others as you want to be treated
rubric: Jesus taught us to do to others what we would have them do to us.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What is stewardship?
options: Caring for what God has entrusted to us|Saving money only|Owning property|Giving orders
answer: Caring for what God has entrusted to us
rubric: Stewardship means managing God's gifts responsibly.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What does render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's teach?
options: Obedience to civil authority|Rebellion against Rome|Avoiding taxes|Worshipping the emperor
rubric: Jesus taught his followers to respect lawful civil authority.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What is humility?
options: Thinking less of yourself and others|Regarding others as better than yourself|Being shy|Being rich
answer: Regarding others as better than yourself
rubric: Humility is putting others first, as Jesus taught.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What is the Christian view of wealth?
options: Wealth is evil|Use it to help others and for God's glory|Wealth proves holiness|Wealth should be hidden
answer: Use it to help others and for God's glory
rubric: Wealth is a trust to be used responsibly and generously.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What is chastity?
options: Purity in sexual conduct|Wealth|Fasting|Prayer
rubric: Chastity is the virtue of purity and self-control.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Which commandment is the first?
options: You shall have no other gods before me|You shall not steal|Honour your parents|You shall not kill
answer: You shall have no other gods before me
rubric: The first commandment forbids worshipping other gods.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What is justice?
options: Giving each person what is rightfully theirs|Punishing everyone|Showing favour to friends|Ignoring the law
answer: Giving each person what is rightfully theirs
rubric: Justice means fairness and giving each person their due.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What does the Bible teach about the love of money?
options: It is the root of all evil|It is a virtue|It is required for salvation|It is harmless
answer: It is the root of all evil
rubric: 1 Timothy 6:10 says the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What happened at Pentecost?
options: The Holy Spirit came upon the apostles|Jesus was born|The temple was built|Peter was arrested
answer: The Holy Spirit came upon the apostles
rubric: At Pentecost the Holy Spirit descended on the apostles.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What appeared above the apostles at Pentecost?
options: Tongues of fire|A rainbow|A dove|A star
rubric: Tongues as of fire appeared and rested on each of them.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Who was the first Christian martyr?
options: Stephen|Peter|Paul|James
rubric: Stephen was stoned to death and became the first martyr.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: On which road was Saul converted?
options: The road to Damascus|The road to Jericho|The road to Emmaus|The road to Rome
rubric: Saul met the risen Jesus on the road to Damascus.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What was Saul's name after his conversion?
options: Paul|Silas|Barnabas|Timothy
rubric: Saul became known as Paul, the apostle to the Gentiles.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: What was the Council of Jerusalem mainly about?
options: Whether Gentiles must keep the Mosaic law|Building a temple|Choosing a king|Paying taxes
answer: Whether Gentiles must keep the Mosaic law
rubric: The council settled that Gentiles were saved by faith, not circumcision.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
stem: Who was the leader of the apostles?
options: Peter|Thomas|Judas|Andrew
rubric: Peter was the leading apostle in the early church.

subject: Civic Education
stem: Who is a citizen?
options: A legally recognised member of a state|A visitor to a country|A foreigner|A trader
answer: A legally recognised member of a state
rubric: A citizen is a legal member of a state with rights and duties.

subject: Civic Education
stem: Which is a way of acquiring Nigerian citizenship?
options: By birth|By wealth|By marriage only|By travelling
rubric: Citizenship can be acquired by birth, registration or naturalisation.

subject: Civic Education
stem: Which of these is a civic responsibility?
options: Paying taxes|Avoiding elections|Ignoring laws|Damaging public property
rubric: Paying taxes is a duty of every citizen.

subject: Civic Education
stem: What does allegiance mean?
options: Loyalty to one's country|Wealth|Freedom|Education
rubric: Allegiance is the loyalty a citizen owes to the state.

subject: Civic Education
stem: What are the colours of the Nigerian flag?
options: Green, white, green|Red, white, red|Green, yellow, green|White, blue, white
rubric: The Nigerian flag has green, white and green vertical bands.

subject: Civic Education
stem: Who designed the Nigerian flag?
options: Taiwo Akinkunmi|Nnamdi Azikiwe|Herbert Macaulay|Obafemi Awolowo
rubric: Taiwo Akinkunmi designed the Nigerian flag in 1959.

subject: Civic Education
stem: When did Nigeria gain independence?
options: 1 October 1960|1 October 1963|27 May 1967|29 May 1999
rubric: Nigeria became independent on 1 October 1960.

subject: Civic Education
stem: When did Nigeria become a republic?
rubric: Nigeria became a republic in 1963 with a president as head of state.

subject: Civic Education
stem: When was the Universal Declaration of Human Rights adopted?
rubric: The UDHR was adopted by the United Nations in 1948.

subject: Civic Education
stem: Which chapter of the Nigerian constitution contains fundamental human rights?
options: Chapter I|Chapter II|Chapter IV|Chapter VII
rubric: Chapter IV of the Nigerian constitution guarantees fundamental rights.

subject: Civic Education
stem: Which is a fundamental human right?
options: Right to life|Right to steal|Right to cheat|Right to disobey the law
rubric: The right to life is guaranteed to every person.

subject: Civic Education
stem: What does fair hearing mean?
options: A fair trial before an impartial court|A quick judgement|A secret trial|A trial without a lawyer
answer: A fair trial before an impartial court
rubric: Fair hearing means a person is given a fair opportunity to defend themselves.

subject: Civic Education
stem: What is freedom of expression?
options: The right to hold and share opinions|The right to fight|The right to travel|The right to own land
answer: The right to hold and share opinions
rubric: Freedom of expression allows citizens to share ideas and opinions.

subject: Civic Education
stem: What is freedom of movement?
options: The right to move freely within the country|The right to leave school|The right to drive|The right to travel abroad without papers
answer: The right to move freely within the country
rubric: Citizens may move and reside anywhere within Nigeria.

subject: Civic Education
stem: Which body promotes human rights in Nigeria?
options: National Human Rights Commission|NNPC|INEC|CBN
rubric: The NHRC protects and promotes human rights in Nigeria.

subject: Civic Education
stem: What does the right to dignity of the human person forbid?
options: Torture and inhuman treatment|Free speech|Movement|Education
rubric: Dignity of the human person forbids torture and degrading treatment.

subject: Civic Education
stem: What is democracy?
options: Government of the people, by the people, for the people|Rule by the army|Rule by one family|Rule by the rich
answer: Government of the people, by the people, for the people
rubric: Democracy is government by the consent of the people.

subject: Civic Education
stem: What is franchise?
options: The right to vote|The right to own land|The right to trade|The right to travel
rubric: Franchise is the legal right to vote in elections.

subject: Civic Education
stem: Which body conducts federal elections in Nigeria?
options: INEC|EFCC|NNPC|NJC
rubric: The Independent National Electoral Commission conducts elections.

subject: Civic Education
stem: What is a secret ballot?
options: Voting without anyone knowing your choice|Voting in secret places|Voting by hand|Voting twice
answer: Voting without anyone knowing your choice
rubric: A secret ballot protects the voter's choice from influence.

subject: Civic Education
stem: What is universal adult suffrage?
options: Every adult citizen has the right to vote|Only men can vote|Only the rich can vote|Only educated people can vote
answer: Every adult citizen has the right to vote
rubric: Universal adult suffrage gives all adults the vote regardless of status.

subject: Civic Education
stem: What is a political party?
options: An organised group seeking political power|A social club|A trade union|A charity
answer: An organised group seeking political power
rubric: Political parties contest elections to form government.

subject: Civic Education
stem: What is a voter's card used for?
options: Identification for voting|Travelling abroad|Opening a bank account|Buying land
rubric: The Permanent Voter Card identifies a registered voter.

subject: Civic Education
stem: What makes an election free and fair?
options: It is conducted without rigging or intimidation|Only one party contests|The army votes|Results are announced late
answer: It is conducted without rigging or intimidation
rubric: Free and fair elections are transparent and free of manipulation.

subject: Civic Education
stem: What does the rule of law mean?
options: Everyone is subject to the law|Only the poor obey the law|Leaders are above the law|Judges make the law
answer: Everyone is subject to the law
rubric: Under the rule of law no one is above the law.

subject: Civic Education
stem: Which is an element of the rule of law?
options: Equality before the law|Rule by force|Secret trials|Immunity for leaders
rubric: All persons are equal before the law.

subject: Civic Education
stem: What is due process?
options: Fair legal procedures that protect rights|A quick judgement|A secret trial|A political rally
answer: Fair legal procedures that protect rights
rubric: Due process ensures fair treatment through the legal system.

subject: Civic Education
stem: What is habeas corpus?
options: An order to bring a detained person to court|A type of election|A tax|A court fine
answer: An order to bring a detained person to court
rubric: Habeas corpus protects against unlawful detention.

subject: Civic Education
stem: Who propounded the theory of separation of powers?
options: Montesquieu|Aristotle|Plato|Rousseau
rubric: Baron de Montesquieu developed the doctrine of separation of powers.

subject: Civic Education
stem: What does separation of powers prevent?
options: Abuse of power|Free speech|Education|Trade
rubric: Dividing power among branches prevents tyranny.

subject: Civic Education
stem: What is an independent judiciary?
options: Judges decide cases without interference|Judges join political parties|Judges obey the president|Judges are elected by soldiers
rubric: An independent judiciary is free from executive control.

subject: Civic Education
stem: What is constitutionalism?
options: Government limited by a constitution|Rule by decree|Rule by one man|Government without law
rubric: Constitutionalism limits government power by law.

subject: Civic Education
stem: What is integrity?
options: Doing what is right even when no one is watching|Being rich|Being popular|Being strong
answer: Doing what is right even when no one is watching
rubric: Integrity is honesty and strong moral principle.

subject: Civic Education
stem: What is patriotism?
options: Love and loyalty to one's country|Hatred of other countries|Wealth|Power
answer: Love and loyalty to one's country
rubric: Patriotism is devotion to one's nation.

subject: Civic Education
stem: What is discipline?
options: Obedience to rules and self-control|Punishment|Wealth|Freedom
rubric: Discipline is training oneself to follow rules and behave well.

subject: Civic Education
stem: Which agency fights corruption in Nigeria?
options: EFCC|NNPC|NTA|CBN
rubric: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission fights corruption.

subject: Civic Education
stem: What is tolerance?
options: Accepting people who differ from you|Agreeing with everyone|Ignoring people|Fighting differences
answer: Accepting people who differ from you
rubric: Tolerance is respect for the views and ways of others.

subject: Civic Education
stem: What is national consciousness?
options: Awareness of belonging to one nation|Love of money|Fear of government|Desire for power
answer: Awareness of belonging to one nation
rubric: National consciousness is a shared sense of national identity.

subject: Civic Education
stem: Which of these is a national value?
options: Hard work|Rigging|Corruption|Tribalism
rubric: Hard work is one of Nigeria's national values.

subject: Civic Education
stem: What is honesty?
options: Being truthful and sincere|Being clever|Being strong|Being rich
rubric: Honesty is the quality of being truthful and upright.

subject: Geography
stem: What are the three main layers of the Earth?
options: Crust, mantle and core|Soil, rock and water|Land, sea and air|Crust, soil and sand
rubric: The Earth is made up of the crust, mantle and core.

subject: Geography
stem: Which is the outermost layer of the Earth?
options: Crust|Mantle|Outer core|Inner core
rubric: The crust is the thin outermost solid layer.

subject: Geography
stem: What is the lithosphere?
options: The crust and upper rigid mantle|The centre of the Earth|The atmosphere|The oceans
answer: The crust and upper rigid mantle
rubric: The lithosphere is the rigid outer shell of the Earth.

subject: Geography
stem: Which rock type is formed from cooled magma?
options: Igneous|Sedimentary|Metamorphic|Limestone
rubric: Igneous rocks form when magma or lava cools and solidifies.

subject: Geography
stem: How long does the Earth take to rotate on its axis?
options: 12 hours|24 hours|365 days|30 days
rubric: One rotation takes about 24 hours and causes day and night.

subject: Geography
stem: How long does the Earth take to revolve round the sun?
options: 24 hours|30 days|365¼ days|100 years
rubric: The Earth completes one revolution in about 365¼ days.

subject: Geography
stem: What is the line of 0° latitude called?
options: Equator|Prime Meridian|Tropic of Cancer|International Date Line
rubric: The equator is the line of latitude at 0°.

subject: Geography
stem: Which instrument records earthquakes?
options: Seismograph|Barometer|Thermometer|Anemometer
rubric: A seismograph detects and records earthquake waves.

subject: Geography
stem: What is a map scale?
options: The ratio between map distance and ground distance|The size of the paper|The direction of north|The height of land
answer: The ratio between map distance and ground distance
rubric: Scale relates distance on the map to real distance on the ground.

subject: Geography
stem: What do contour lines join?
options: Points of equal height above sea level|Points of equal rainfall|Points of equal temperature|Points of equal population
answer: Points of equal height above sea level
rubric: Contours show relief by joining points of equal elevation.

subject: Geography
stem: What does a scale of 1:50,000 mean?
options: 1 cm on the map represents 50,000 cm on the ground|1 km represents 50 km|1 cm represents 50 cm|1 m represents 50 m
answer: 1 cm on the map represents 50,000 cm on the ground
rubric: The representative fraction compares map units to ground units.

subject: Geography
stem: What is a grid reference used for?
options: Locating places on a map|Measuring rainfall|Finding temperature|Measuring wind
rubric: Grid references give the exact position of features on a map.

subject: Geography
stem: What is true north?
options: The direction of the North Pole|The direction of the sun|The direction of the equator|The direction of the wind
answer: The direction of the North Pole
rubric: True north points to the geographic North Pole.

subject: Geography
stem: What is relief on a map?
options: The shape and height of the land|The colour of the map|The scale of the map|The title of the map
answer: The shape and height of the land
rubric: Relief describes the hills, valleys and heights of the land.

subject: Geography
stem: What is a cross-section?
options: A side view of the land along a line on a map|A type of map|A map symbol|A scale
answer: A side view of the land along a line on a map
rubric: A cross-section shows the profile of the land between two points.

subject: Geography
stem: What is weather?
options: Atmospheric conditions over a short period|Average weather over many years|The height of land|The study of rocks
answer: Atmospheric conditions over a short period
rubric: Weather changes daily, unlike climate.

subject: Geography
stem: What is climate?
options: Average weather over many years|Daily temperature|Rainfall today|Wind direction now
rubric: Climate is the long-term average of weather.

subject: Geography
stem: Which instrument measures temperature?
options: Thermometer|Barometer|Rain gauge|Anemometer
rubric: A thermometer measures air temperature.

subject: Geography
stem: Which instrument measures rainfall?
options: Rain gauge|Hygrometer|Barometer|Wind vane
rubric: A rain gauge collects and measures rainfall.

subject: Geography
stem: Which instrument measures air pressure?
options: Barometer|Thermometer|Anemometer|Rain gauge
rubric: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure.

subject: Geography
stem: Which instrument measures wind speed?
options: Anemometer|Barometer|Hygrometer|Thermometer
rubric: An anemometer measures the speed of the wind.

subject: Geography
stem: What is convectional rainfall?
options: Rainfall caused by heated air rising and cooling|Rainfall caused by mountains|Rainfall caused by fronts|Rainfall caused by wind
answer: Rainfall caused by heated air rising and cooling
rubric: Heated air rises, cools and condenses to form rain.

subject: Geography
stem: What is the harmattan?
options: A dry dusty wind from the Sahara|A heavy rainstorm|A type of soil|A river in Nigeria
answer: A dry dusty wind from the Sahara
rubric: The harmattan is a dry, dusty wind that blows over West Africa.

subject: Geography
stem: How is population density calculated?
options: Population divided by land area|Births minus deaths|Population times area|People plus houses
rubric: Density is the number of people per unit area.

subject: Geography
stem: What is a census?
options: An official count of a population|A type of map|A weather record|A rock sample
answer: An official count of a population
rubric: A census counts and records details of a population.

subject: Geography
stem: What is birth rate?
options: Live births per 1,000 people per year|Deaths per 1,000 people|People per square kilometre|Number of migrants
answer: Live births per 1,000 people per year
rubric: Birth rate measures live births in a population each year.

subject: Geography
stem: What is death rate?
options: Deaths per 1,000 people per year|Births per 1,000 people|People per square kilometre|Number of houses
rubric: Death rate measures deaths in a population each year.

subject: Geography
stem: What is natural increase?
options: Birth rate minus death rate|Birth rate plus death rate|Population divided by area|Migration into a country
rubric: Natural increase is the surplus of births over deaths.

subject: Geography
stem: What is migration?
options: Movement of people from one place to another|Growth of a city|A type of rainfall|A rock formation
answer: Movement of people from one place to another
rubric: Migration is the movement of people between places.

subject: Geography
stem: What is rural-urban migration?
options: Movement from villages to cities|Movement from cities to villages|Movement abroad|Movement within a village
rubric: People move to cities seeking jobs and better services.

subject: Geography
stem: What is overpopulation?
options: When population exceeds available resources|When a country is large|When many people are old|When birth rate falls
rubric: Overpopulation occurs when resources cannot support the people.

subject: Geography
stem: Which country borders Nigeria to the west?
options: Benin Republic|Niger Republic|Cameroon|Chad
rubric: Benin Republic lies to the west of Nigeria.

subject: Geography
stem: Which country borders Nigeria to the north?
options: Niger Republic|Benin Republic|Cameroon|Ghana
rubric: Niger Republic shares Nigeria's northern border.

subject: Geography
stem: At which town do the Niger and Benue rivers meet?
options: Lokoja|Onitsha|Makurdi|Jebba
rubric: The Niger and Benue meet at Lokoja, forming a confluence.

subject: Geography
stem: What is the highest point in Nigeria?
options: Chappal Waddi|Zuma Rock|Oban Hills|Jos Plateau
rubric: Chappal Waddi in Taraba State is Nigeria's highest peak.

subject: Geography
stem: Which vegetation zone has dense trees and heavy rainfall?
options: Rainforest|Savanna|Sahel|Desert
rubric: The rainforest has tall dense trees and heavy rainfall.

subject: Geography
stem: What is the savanna?
options: Tropical grassland with scattered trees|Dense forest|A desert|A swamp
rubric: Savanna is grassland with scattered trees, common in Nigeria.

subject: Geography
stem: How many states are there in Nigeria?
rubric: Nigeria has 36 states plus the Federal Capital Territory.

subject: Geography
stem: Which region of Nigeria produces most crude oil?
options: Niger Delta|Jos Plateau|Sokoto|Kano
rubric: The Niger Delta is Nigeria's main oil-producing region.

subject: Geography
stem: What is the capital of Nigeria?
options: Abuja|Lagos|Kano|Ibadan
rubric: Abuja became Nigeria's capital in 1991.
